answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments and verifiable delay primitives form a robust thread of protection against identity cloning, analogous to the opal-like opacity of such schemes in securing the kernel of decentralized systems, by iteratively binding and verifying the reputation of autonomous agents, thereby precluding computational attempts to forge identities, as the sequential delay function ensures that any attempts to clone an identity are detectable through the accumulation of delayed verifications.
